perItemFindings.one_line: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

verbatim_critique: [D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=incremental below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The note proves branch influence-function classes, their intersection-based convolution lower bound, finite Gram criteria, and an explicit strict-gap witness, but it does not prove that any estimator attains the union bound. Consequently, the advertised oracle-adaptation frontier characterizes equality of abstract variance bounds rather than existence of a procedure that adapts to either branch at those bounds. The negative uniformity theorem exploits arbitrary finite-coordinate splicing in the chosen sequence class and does not resolve feasibility on a conventional uniformly controlled local neighborhood. The results are further confined to fixed finite support and strict-interior constant-rank intersections, and they supply neither implementable inference nor evidence that the diagnostic improves either cited application. These omissions keep the package below a field-level econometrics contribution and constrain its projected journal score despite the framing prose generally disclosing them. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.3 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
